# Pandamonium v1.0.55

This patch completes the M13 plugin capability discovery and repository intake program: extensions installed before capability inventories existed now rebuild theirs on read, and the operator and agent flows are documented alongside the end-to-end intake proof.

## MAD-916 — Extensions: backfill capability inventory and prove intake acceptance

### Problem

Extensions installed before MAD-912 introduced the persisted capability inventory had no metadata for `manage_extensions action=inspect`, so their capabilities stayed invisible even though the agent query and mount paths existed. The program also lacked an end-to-end lifecycle proof and operator documentation.

### Implementation

Registry reads now backfill a missing inventory from the record's already-validated effective capabilities and admitted skills, without re-running any adapter. Tampered or stale inventories still fail closed, and disabled legacy records without effective metadata remain without an inventory until they are enabled, upgraded, or reinstalled. Adds `tests/test_extension_intake_end_to_end.py` covering static scan → source plan → approval → execute → persisted inventory and effective capability readback, and `docs/jos-extension-intake-runtime.md` covering the agent capability query, the Add-from-GitHub operator flow, backfill behavior, limits, and verification commands.

### Product value and UI visibility

Operators upgrading an existing installation no longer start with an empty capability view: every enabled plugin answers `manage_extensions action=inspect` immediately, and the Add Plugins → Add from GitHub flow (shipped in v1.0.54) keeps its staged scan, review, and approval surfaces unchanged. The new runtime document gives the agent and operator flows one canonical reference.

### Verification

`tests/test_extension_capability_inventory_persistence.py` (legacy backfill and disabled legacy cases) and `tests/test_extension_intake_end_to_end.py`; full suite 5764 passed / 5 skipped. The v1.0.54 release already ships the user-facing intake flow (MAD-911/913/914/915); this patch adds the backfill and documentation on top.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No schema, API, dependency, or authority change. Backfill happens on registry read and is derived only from data the registry already validated; disabled legacy extensions need an enable, upgrade, or reinstall before their inventory exists. Rollback is reverting the MAD-916 commit; no data is migrated or deleted.
